operator_io_quirks: All 7 tables are tiny (15 rows each); no huge-table sampling needed, but read_schema must still handle max_rows_per_table path.
Table names are mixed-case with underscores (Customers, Order_Items, Shipment_Items); DDL uses backticks, not double quotes — writer must emit double-quoted identifiers and sqlite accepts both.
Shipment_Items has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to dedupe.
Shipment_Items is a pure junction table with two FKs and no PK — duplicate (shipment_id, order_item_id) pairs are legal and present upstream.
All FKs point to existing parents with unique PKs; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite keys, no non-unique parents.

Declared DATETIME columns (invoice_date, date_order_placed, shipment_date) store TEXT in format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' — Date fuzzer template must be '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' (not the 7 upstream templates' date-only forms); first element does not parse as int so Date branch is taken, not Number.

VARCHAR(10) status columns (order_status, order_item_status) hold short enum-like text ('Shipped','Packing','On Road','Finish','Payed','Cancel') — String fuzzer with length range [min,max+1] from elements.

shipment_tracking_number is VARCHAR(80) but stores digit-only strings ('3452','0114','478') — String fuzzer will treat as int-like and add str(i±1) neighbours; storage class text contradicts numeric-looking content.

Four columns are 100% NULL in the original (order_details, product_details, order_item_details, other_shipment_details) with distinct=0 — original_values is all-None, so Base drops them and p:=1 (always fresh).

customer_id in Orders has distinct=10 < 15 rows: FK fan-in, not a uniqueness violation; Shipments.invoice_number distinct=7, Shipments.order_id distinct=12, Order_Items.product_id distinct=9, Order_Items.order_id distinct=9 — all FK fan-in.
All PKs are INTEGER single-column; Number fuzzer with scale=0 (no args) → range [-1,1] then perturb ±1/±2, so fresh PKs collide often and sample_fresh_primary_keys will drop many rows.

NOT NULL columns: Orders.customer_id/order_status/date_order_placed, Order_Items.product_id/order_id/order_item_status, Shipments.order_id/invoice_number, Shipment_Items.shipment_id/order_item_id — upstream does not enforce NOT NULL in Python; NULL rows fail at insert and are skipped.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on the three DATETIME columns: template inferred from first parsable element = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; range = [min,max] of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 1971..2010), so fresh dates cluster in that window — plausible but narrow.
Number fuzzer on all INTEGER PKs: scale=0, range [-1,1], perturb ±1/±2 → tiny integer space; with 15-row tables and PK dedupe, many rows dropped, final table sizes well below chosen size.

String fuzzer on VARCHAR(80/255) name/detail columns: length range from 5 sampled originals (e.g. [4,9] for customer_name), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() → random gibberish names, plus 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop) — implausible values drive FN on name-equality predicates.

String fuzzer on order_status/order_item_status (VARCHAR(10)): length range from 3 distinct short values, so fresh strings are 3-10 chars of gibberish — status='Shipped' predicates almost never match → FN.
String fuzzer on shipment_tracking_number: elements are digit strings, so int-like branch adds str(i±1); fresh draws are alphanumeric gibberish — tracking-number equality predicates miss.

100%-NULL columns: Base drops all None elements → p:=1, always fresh String draws; original has zero non-null values so any predicate on these columns is trivially empty in original but TS fills them → FP risk on IS NULL / IS NOT NULL.

FK consistency: child columns draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; with tiny parent sizes after PK dedupe, FK fan-in is preserved but absolute counts shrink — join cardinalities differ from original.
Shipment_Items has no PK and no unique columns: no dedupe, so duplicate (shipment_id, order_item_id) pairs are generated freely — COUNT(*) on the junction table inflates vs original.
Number fuzzer quirk (list_max overwritten to full-range max) is irrelevant here since all INTEGER columns have no (a,b) args and scale=0.
p=0.2 default with 30% chance of p=0 for whole instance: when p=0, Date fuzzer returns fresh dates always (inverted p), String returns fresh always — more implausible values.
max_l0 cap (rng.random()*30) applies to non-PK columns; single-column PKs get inf, so PKs keep drawing fresh tiny ints and colliding — heavy PK dedupe.

Known misses: FN from gibberish strings/statuses and narrow date windows; FP from filling 100%-NULL columns and from junction-table duplicates; ties/duplicates in FK fan-in are preserved by with-replacement draw.
